prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 5.25. Exact Sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।
छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ २५ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Seers who have eliminated their impurities, whose doubts have been cut through, who are self-restrained, and who are devoted to the welfare of all beings — they attain nirvāṇa in Brahman. Chapter context: Renunciation and action, equanimity, freedom from attachment and inner peace. Use the verse-specific person, comparison or natural metaphor rather than generic grand divinity. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: One who is happy within, who finds delight within, who is illumined within — that yogi, becoming Brahman, attains nirvāṇa in Brahman. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: For the self-disciplined ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who have restrained the mind and have known the Self — brahma-nirvāṇa surrounds them on all sides. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.25: Seers who have eliminated their impurities, whose doubts have been cut through, who are self-restrained, and who are devoted to the welfare of all beings — they attain nirvāṇa in Brahman.
